I have been working this land for 40 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is good but dry without irrigation, so my well is everything.

My 30 mu: I run wheat and maize on 22 mu as a rotation — same fields, wheat in winter, maize in summer. I keep 8 mu for stevia separately. My son pushed me to grow stevia a few years back when the price was high and buyers come to the village now. I keep it.

**Wheat:** I plant in October after deep ploughing. I use the improved variety from the seed station — yields better than the old seed I saved. I put base fertilizer down at planting, then top-dress urea at jointing. I irrigate at sowing, jointing, heading, and once more if grain fill looks dry — usually 3 to 4 times. Two pesticide sprays: one for aphids, one fungicide around heading.

**Maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June. I use hybrid seed — everyone around here does now, the yield difference is real. Rotary till after wheat straw, then plant. Fertilize at planting and side-dress at big bell stage. Two or three irrigations: at silking, grain fill, and one more if August is hot. One or two pesticide passes for corn borer mostly.

**Stevia:** It stays in the same 8 mu. I prepare with rotary tillage in spring. It needs more water than grain — I irrigate 5 or 6 times through the growing season. I harvest leaves twice, dry them, and sell to the buyer who comes to town. It earns more per mu than wheat or maize.

With some family off-farm, I manage the heavy work with hired help at planting and harvest.
